label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: logs COMPLETE, timings COMPLETE, handler max 905.108 ms, failures 0

report.summary: Outbox publications fell to ~10 per 10 s while arrivals stayed at 22, so pending grew. Slow consumer handler responses (~905 ms) coincide with the lower throughput. The consumer slowness itself is unexplained.

findings.claim: Outbox publication rate fell below arrival rate from the 7th bucket on, building a backlog (pending 1 to 198).
findings.reason: Arrivals stay at 22 per bucket while publications drop to about 10 per bucket; pending rises.

findings.claim: The consumer handler is slow on a subset of deliveries (p95 905 ms, p50 0.025 ms). This accounts for the p95 total of 984 ms.
findings.reason: Auth (~70 ms) and unattributed time are small; handler time dominates the tail.

findings.claim: Slow consumer responses limit delivery throughput, which delays notifications. Roughly 1 s per delivery would give the observed ~10 per 10 s.
findings.reason: Throughput matches serial ~1 s deliveries within poll and batch settings; this is not directly confirmed.

findings.claim: Transfer API, DB pool and DB locking are healthy and are not the cause. All deliveries succeeded, with no timeouts or errors.
findings.reason: No 5xx, zero pool pending or timeouts, no blocking, and 509/509 delivery successes.

limitations: No consumer-side logs or per-attempt time series, so the onset of slow handler responses cannot be aligned with the throughput drop.
Throughput limits from serial delivery are inferred, not measured; only the first 100 delivery records are listed.
next_checks: Inspect consumer handler latency over time and why it takes ~900 ms for some requests.
Check whether the outbox poller delivers serially and how the 778 old FAILED rows were produced.

alternatives.reason: The failed count stays at 778 for the whole window and the oldest age grows only with the clock; it is static.
alternatives.hypothesis: The 778 FAILED outbox rows (age ~11 h) are a separate older problem and not the cause of the current delay.

alternatives.reason: Handler time sits on the consumer side, and the pool shows no contention.
alternatives.hypothesis: LedgerCore's own poller is slow, rather than the consumer.
